speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Education with regard to the recent Sengkang Green Primary bullying case, what further steps have the Ministry taken to strengthen anti-bullying measures and ensure timely support for both victims and perpetrators, including mental health resources.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether there is a Ministry or cluster level framework in place on how schools should deal with bullying cases; and (b) whether the Ministry encourages schools to share and develop best practices of dealing with bullying cases among themselves.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether schools are adequately resourced to prevent the occurrences of bullying incidents in schools; (b) whether there are proactive monitoring and surveillance to pick up early signs of bullying situations; and (c) what further preventive measures can be taken.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how will the Ministry equip schools and teachers to detect and respond to multifaceted forms of bullying; and (b) how will the Ministry ensure consistency and accountability of all parties across institutions.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry will consider adopting more aspects of evidence-based anti-bullying programmes such as intervention teams; (b) what new measures are being considered to further empower victims and bystanders to report bullying incidents safely; and (c) whether there are plans to enhance support systems, such peer support groups, for students affected by bullying.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen
text: asked the Minister for Education how many reported school bullying cases in the past three years involved suspected or confirmed child maltreatment of either the perpetrator or victim of bullying, in light of the impact that a family environment has on a child’s behaviour.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry will consider setting up a centralised anti-bullying unit to support schools to investigate the most egregious cases of bullying and follow up with disciplinary and rehabilitative actions, so as to avoid overburdening teachers; and (b) if not, why not.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what resources are available to schools to detect and counter less visible forms of bullying such as manipulation, exclusion and cyberbullying; (b) how does the Ministry support teachers in managing bullying cases; and (c) what measures beyond training are implemented to ensure teachers have the time and resources to address bullying without adding to their risk of burnout.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen
text: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee): Mr Speaker, Sir, my response will address the questions raised by Members on the management of bullying incidents in schools.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: My response will also cover related oral and written questions filed both for earlier as well as subsequent Sittings from Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Dr Charlene Chen, Mr Kenneth Tiong, Mr David Hoe, Mr Xie Yao Quan, Ms Joan Pereira, Ms Hany Soh, Dr Wan Rizal, Ms Jessica Tan, Ms Mariam Jaafar, Ms He Ting Ru, Mr Gerald Giam, Ms Yeo Wan Ling1, Mr Foo Cexiang, Ms Eileen Chong and Ms Elysa Chen.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I invite Members to seek clarifications, if needed and thereafter, withdraw their questions for subsequent Sittings.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We place a strong emphasis on providing a safe environment in our schools so that our students can learn, grow and thrive.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We know that such incidents affect many people.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Children who experience hurtful behaviour may worry about their safety and may find it hard to learn and build friendships.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Parents love their children and naturally feel anxious and concerned about the children's well-being, whether they have been affected by bullying or have been themselves involved in hurting others.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For our school leaders, teachers and school staff, these incidents require them to manage disruptive behaviours in order to restore discipline.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They have to protect those affected, rebuild a safe learning environment and address and correct those involved in wrong behaviours.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They seek to help our students learn from their mistakes while engaging with parents who might hold different perspectives on how schools ought to respond.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our approach seeks to provide practical support to help children learn better behaviour, give parents confidence in school responses and enable teachers to maintain caring and enabling learning environments for all students.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Schools have rules against such behaviours and teach students why these behaviours are wrong.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, we recognise that children learn behaviours from multiple sources – home, school, peers, online.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Therefore, upstream preventive work involves these parties, and we all need to play a part.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Third, discipline in the context of the school environment is an educative process.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Disciplinary measures must help students learn the consequences of their actions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As children have the potential to learn from their mistakes and grow through experience, our disciplinary approach must continue to focus on teaching, guiding and rehabilitating our children, and helping to restore relationships.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We need to work with them, build a relationship with them so that they can work with us to instill kindness and respect for others through positive adult role modelling, and closer monitoring of children's online activities, especially outside school.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our schools also work with the community and partners in addressing hurtful behaviours.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some Members asked about the outcomes of previous reviews.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Of these, three were relevant to strengthening schools' capacity to address hurtful behaviours and bullying.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, the CCE curriculum was refreshed to place stronger emphasis on guiding students to be kind and caring, both online as well as offline.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, sometimes, when you go around, you see some of the children with a badge that says "Peer Support Leader", or some other variant of the name.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Third, our schools have designated staff whose work covers areas such as fostering positive school culture, addressing hurtful behaviours and working with parents and the community to guide and educate our students.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I will next elaborate on how these enhancements and other existing measures address bullying and hurtful behaviours in our schools.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: From young, our students learn pro-social behaviours through lessons and adult role-modelling in schools.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The CCE curriculum and the school environment emphasise values and respect, and students learn to be kind to their classmates, resolve disagreements respectfully and learn appropriate ways to stand up against bullying.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Through cyber wellness lessons, they also learn to extend such pro-social behaviours online.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In addition, students learn about healthy mindsets, habits and skills to strengthen their mental health and resilience in the face of challenges.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Students learn how to respond when they encounter unsafe situations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They are taught to stay calm, avoid retaliation, move away from the situation and seek help from a trusted adult, such as their parents, teachers or school leaders.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some Members asked about school processes such as anti-bullying frameworks, reporting channels, investigation, parent engagement timelines and disciplinary measures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our schools have policies and frameworks that send a clear message to students that hurtful behaviours and bullying are not acceptable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These include school rules and consequences for bullying.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are also various reporting channels for students to report bullying.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, students can report incidents directly or through their friends, peer support leaders, teachers and school leaders, or through online platforms such as emails or online forms.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Discipline talks for students are also conducted regularly by schools to communicate their approach to managing misconduct, including bullying.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When an incident is reported, our schools conduct investigations before deciding on the appropriate course of action which includes disciplinary as well as restorative actions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These measures help students learn from their mistakes, reframe their thinking and change their behaviours.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When bullying occurs, our priority is the safety of the affected students.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This could include separating them from perpetrators, facilitating the removal of hurtful online content and identifying peer support leaders to befriend and look out for them in school.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In addition, teachers and school counsellors work with both victims and perpetrators. helping them manage their emotions and work towards mending ties and restoring friendships.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Students who continue to experience distress are referred to community resources, such as the Response, Early Intervention and Assessment in Community Mental Health (REACH) teams for more specialised support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I will just pause here to mention that I am using the words "perpetrator" and "victim" in order to shorten the phrases, but I know people might be concerned about the labels that we use – and certainly we are mindful of that – and we continue to see how best we can find the right terms to use both in public discourse as well as in our institutions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, please bear with us in the meantime.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I would also say, Sir, that parent engagement and partnership are vital.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When bullying incidents happen, schools engage parents to inform them about the facts of the incident, work with them on the safety plan and focus on the well-being of the students.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The time it takes to investigate each case will vary, depending on complexity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Similarly, restoring and mending relationships and improving behaviour, take time and parents are encouraged to work with schools and give this process some time to take effect.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Schools share resources with parents and parent support groups on how to form caring relationships and monitor their children's online behaviour, online activities and tips to support the children in cases of bullying and cyberbullying.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I have a printed copy of the "Parenting for Wellness Toolbox" for parents, which is put together by MOE, the Health Promotion Board (HPB) and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are some chapters here on, for example, cyberbullying: when a child is the victim, what can parents do?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: How to notice signs and symptoms that the child might have been cyberbullied both in and outside of school, how to engage in conversation with the children and then, of course, when your child is himself or herself involved in causing hurtful behaviour against others.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As part of teacher preparation courses, all teachers are trained to foster positive class culture, address hurtful behaviours and recognise signs of distress.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They are supported by key personnel and school counsellors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our schools use MOE guidelines and resources on what constitutes bullying and cyberbullying, and how to manage these cases.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some schools also work with social service agencies (SSAs) to conduct bullying and cyberbullying awareness programmes for students and training workshops for school staff.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: School personnel also regularly review their school-based strategies to manage bullying and share good practices with other schools.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Indeed, improving our framework to tackle bullying is a continual work-in-progress.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members have raised useful suggestions that we will consider as we seek to strengthen our current measures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Based on the work done so far, we are now conducting external public consultation on four key areas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, strengthening our school culture, environment and processes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, give greater emphasis to values education for our students.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Third, providing more resources and support for our schools and educators and deepening their capacity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Fourth, enhancing school-home partnerships, the relationship between our teachers and educators, and parents and families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are encouraged to have received many constructive suggestions from parents, students, educators, community partners and researchers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our shared goal as an education system and as a society must be an empowering one.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have a collective responsibility to help our children, our next generation, learn how to relate to others, be kind and show respect to others.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They may make mistakes when they were performing the co-curricular activities (CCAs).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They may make mistakes in their project work.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And they may make mistakes in their interpersonal relationships with others, both with their teachers as well as other schoolmates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some of these could be inadvertent or careless behaviour, lack of awareness or sensitivity.

Ultimately, we want to keep improving and enhancing our system, addressing the concerns of parents, the workload on our educators and their sense of mission; and of course, addressing the issues that the public raised.
We all want the same outcome: for schools to be safe, caring and enabling environments for all students and our staff.

MOE will continue to work with schools, parents, community professionals and members of the public as we collectively role model the right behaviours and create the gracious and respectful society for our children to flourish.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As a parent, when I first heard the news about bullying and how persistent it has been over the past few months, it was extremely worrying.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As an educator and someone who believes strongly in mental health, I thought we were on the right track, scaffolding our efforts to make sure that we give the right support to the children.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: But being a parent too, and many parents have actually approached me about the concern of whether we are being a bit too soft in our approach, and whether a harder stance would be necessary.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As an educator, I also feel that, sometimes as educators, we do not have that empowerment to take extra steps further.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Of course, we worry about the effects of us being too hard on our students sometimes, but I think it is a balance.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Having said that, I have two supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And I think we need to have more support.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As an educator, I have mentioned before about our worries about being sidelined for taking a harder stance on some students, for example.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I can see where the Member is coming from, both as an educator as well as a parent.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First on empowering parents, sharing with them best practices, sharing with them the toolkits – I have explained earlier in my response how our schools already do that and how some of these materials are available both online and sometimes in hard copy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But I think we should spend this quality time looking at how we can further enhance and improve our system to address the concerns of children, parents and of the public, while also making sure that we assure our educators and our school staff who are on the frontlines, teaching, not just teaching academic knowledge, but also shaping, teaching and moulding lives, values and perspectives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There were some ideas that were given through the review, including the dialogue that I hosted.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A parent shared that in the school that her daughter was in, the school would, at the start of every academic year, have some material circulated to every parent, and this is over and on top of what is already being done across most schools and by MOE.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is what we call the community learning network, where we have our educators from different tracks share their best practices with one another, so that we continue this spirit of positive learning on how to manage various issues on the ground as well as in the community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, that is first, and we certainly would value ideas from the Member as well as other Members on how better we can support parents, work with our schools and with our teachers to manage these issues, whether the child is a recipient of hurtful behaviour, or is the person who affects others through his or her behaviour.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And some discipline masters have also shared with me that they make some adjustments along the way.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, they may find that it is more effective to make the child perform some community work in the school as opposed to just suspending the child and the child does not learn and the child might not see that really as punishment, in certain circumstances.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, when these are done appropriately, and we leave some judgement to the educators and school leaders, these will help eventually for our children to learn and to grow.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: And I thank the Minister for his response.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Allow me to say that my three questions come from conversations with various Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: First and foremost, it is about disciplinary measures.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Reason being because suspension during my time was painful because you do not get to interact with your friends and even if you go to the arcade, you have to be home by 6.30 pm.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: But parents do highlight to me that with the access of mobile phones today, a home suspension just means that at home, they can play Mobile Legend.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: This then makes us question the effectiveness of home suspension.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: So, could MOE consider moving from home suspension to in-house suspension?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The second question comes from the fact about the well-being and the safety of the person that is reporting.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: And the third point is about accessible channels.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: I recognise that there are a few accessible channels mentioned earlier, but we wonder whether could MOE consider specifying a minimum bundle of reporting options, such as those mentioned earlier, peer support, online reporting and so on, so that this allows schools to have a common baseline and every child in all schools will know that these are the various tools that they can access, while still allowing schools to retain their autonomy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They apply it based on the circumstances and based on the children concerned.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This idea of suspension, the feedback that the Member has given to us is also feedback we have received for some children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Suspension from school, sometimes, is also a safety measure to separate the children and ask the child concerned to not come to class, it can be viewed differently.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For some children, they feel that this is a consequence that they learn from.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One, an anti-retaliation clause, another on accessible bundle of channels.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I will take it in the spirit, as I mentioned earlier, that the Member's views, as well as those of other Members, will be studied and considered.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There are many Members who wish to ask questions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will only call on those who have filed Parliamentary Questions (PQs) on this subject.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I also request that everyone keep your supplementary questions short so that we can cover as many PQs in the course of today.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: First, to what extent is there the close monitoring of the victims as well as the perpetrators after the bullying – on the part of victims, when it comes to adherence to the safety plan; and for the perpetrators, the adherence to any long-term interventions and rehabilitation?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Second is, in terms of the existing review that is ongoing, where does the Minister or the Ministry see as the current gaps that need to be further strengthened and when can we expect these to be announced?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Well, the schools will do that after consequences are meted out or counselling and other measures are brought into place and depending on the situation, of course, and depending on the impact of the children, the educators, the school counsellors necessary, or sometimes even external agencies like REACH, may be called in and each will have to be customised based on the situation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Louis Chua and Minister Desmond Lee have set the gold standard in terms of their clarifications and replies.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In this regard, I wish to ask how promptly do the schools or the teachers get in touch with the parents?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Is it once the bullying incident had occurred, to update the parents at the earliest opportunity, and whether there will be continuous efforts to handhold and work with the parents in addressing the issues?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I think, many a times, while we acknowledge and understand that resources are lean, and teachers and schools are working very hard in addressing different issues at the same time, it does comes in useful to assure the parents on the progress and hard work that have been undertaken by the teachers and the schools in their best efforts to address the issue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And if a safety plan needs to be put in place, it will be done.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Then, some fact-finding – what happened, who were involved and so on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And in deciding whether and when to contact parents, sometimes, there are one-off incidents in class, where children have an altercation or some hurtful words were said, and the teacher's teaching and the teacher wants to restore discipline, turn it into a learning opportunity and then carry on with the rest of the class.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And sometimes, the teachers might then say, it has been addressed between two or three children, one-off, they might then decide they do not really need to get the parents involved.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But sometimes the issue is more serious or if it is a repeat issue, the teachers, of course, apart from tackling safety and then doing some quick fact-finding, will then notify the parents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is a judgement that the key personnel for student well-being, as well as the teachers and the school leaders have to exercise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Of course, when they notify the parents, they would notify all sides who were involved, in order to tell them what has happened so that they also hear from the school and then, of course, on the follow-up action the school will take.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And of course, working with the parents to make sure that the learning points are carried across both in the classroom as well as at home.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I also like to ask the Minister if he can share what support measures are in place for students who have been identified as victims or perpetrators of bullying who also experience child maltreatment at home?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And also, how does the Ministry ensure that teachers and school staff are trained to recognise signs of child maltreatment linked to bullying cases?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My last question: because we understand that each case is varying in complexity, can the Ministry provide an average timeframe for resolution to report to closure in bullying cases that have been reported across schools?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The second question is, whether does MOE also carry out some of these psychological studies or research, to better look out for the kind of profile of students who are likely to bully others and those that are likely to be bullied, so that it can be instructive for the educators on how to look out for indications and signs that bullying could happen?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Whether schools do postmortem, well, it depends on what has happened.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But I am confident that the schools do look-backs just as they share best practices with one another, both within the school as well as across various schools and clusters.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, I think, the Member is asking whether we look at the background of students or have some circumstances based on social work practices where we look out for possible signs and symptoms.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, it is not just consequences and then help them to learn.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We need to try to ascertain what are the underlying causes that lead to this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If it is a repeat issue, does the child have special needs that may cause them to react in a certain way, for which, certain course of action is needed to support the child?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Is it due to poor role modelling, maybe outside school?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I think that is the deeper work that not just our educators but also that of the school counsellors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Sometimes, if it manifests itself in long-term absenteeism, our school welfare officers will also get involved.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, in terms of the actual best practice implementation, is there some consistency and accountability across all institutions?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: And second, while it is extremely difficult, what training or help is given to both students and teachers in terms of early identification of bullying cases?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: It is extremely difficult in some cases, but is there training or support given so that there could be early identification and therefore, early intervention?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, as I mentioned earlier, there is an MOE framework, the School Bullying Management Guidelines that is issued to schools where they set out some guidelines for schools in order to help them implement their measures effectively in school.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is a community learning network – sometimes, it involves the discipline masters; sometimes, school leaders for different topics, they also have these learning networks for various subjects as well and CCA and CCE, and so on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, when it comes to managing hurtful behaviour, bullying in schools, there is also such a network among teachers as well as key personnel who are involved in our schools in handling these issues.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, is that training and help for early identification that would apply across the board in the school, from school leader to educator to counsellor and school welfare officers to our students.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A lot of it is enmeshed into our CCE classes that bring across these points in an age-appropriate way.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, in primary school, lower primary, we teach them about friendship: how to make friends, how to maintain friendships, how to be kind, caring and sensitive to one another.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And as you grow a little bit older, it will be a bit more explicit about hurtful and bullying behaviours and then how to be an upstander, how to respond appropriately and how to look out for cyberbullying, and so on.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, that is for the school at large.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Then, of course, we have peer support leaders and that was a result of the 2020 major CCE framework review.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Peer support leaders do not just deal with bullying and hurtful behaviours, of course, they are there to help students who have difficulty adjusting, new students who have come in, primary one students, help to keep an eye out for other students who might run into difficulties or may feel down and of course, to look out for early signs of bullying and then trained to report to an appropriate adult, including a teacher or a counsellor.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have got two supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For cases of cyberbullying, what is the status of the Ministry's work with relevant authorities and online platforms to take action on cyberbullying incidents or content?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And my second question, do these include quick-response channels that will allow the rapid take down of bullying content posted online?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But at the school-level, if it is one child posting about another child, then it will involve, at the school-level, asking the children concerned to take it down as part of the resolution process.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As for quick-reporting channels, I believe that I mentioned earlier that some schools have online forms, contact arrangements and reporting channels for them to report bullying, including cyberbullying.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: Speaker, I go to the question that I filed, suggesting the set-up of a centralised anti-bullying unit to support schools to not only investigate the most egregious cases of bullying, but also to follow up with disciplinary and rehabilitative actions with the key purpose of avoiding overburdening our teachers.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
text: And I would just like to ask the Minister if that is one of the specific measures being considered under the review?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If I may share, during our engagements, we also received a similar suggestion.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our teachers are there to teach, but when incidents happen, they want to restore discipline so teaching can continue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But even in dealing with these bad behaviours, as I said, children make mistakes on their academic work, project work and there is corrective and remedial action needed from a pedagogical point of view.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But also when it comes to certain behaviours that they manifest in the classroom, in trying to restore classroom discipline, it is also a teachable moment for the students.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Having said that, when matters escalate or if it is more serious, key personnel in the school may be involved.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, of course, we have to study this carefully, because if we bring these people in, they will have to then integrate well with what is happening in our schools.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The teachers on the ground know the children well and also understand the dynamics.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If we bring in an external party, they have expertise, but they will then also have to go through a certain get-up in order to understand what is going on and to build the relationship with the school, educators and staff as well as with the parents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I have two supplementary questions raised by educators.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And secondly, in strengthening anti-bullying measures, how does the Ministry strike a balance between protecting victims and helping students build resilience to manage everyday small disagreements or teasing that may not amount to bullying?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: I mean, for small issues or incidents that may not be considered as bullying, but students report it to teachers and teachers may be overwhelmed by some of these small incidents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I understand where the Member is coming from.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I think, sometimes you can never get it perfect because so many children are involved and we have this network of peer support leaders as well, and all our children are encouraged to report if there are issues that they face.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They are not feeling good, or they see some other classmate in difficulty or they see some behaviours, they will report, because they look up to the teacher as someone whom they respect, as a figure of authority, someone whom they know and trust, and the teacher will then exercise judgement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I do not think there is a particular policy you can put in place to get children, including primary school children, to calibrate it to the right level.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we are mindful, ultimately, of the demands on our teachers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They are prepared to work hard, but there must be clear purpose and meaning, and helping our children learn the right values and the right behaviours, and building resilience in them is important, comparable to what they are teaching in terms of academic subjects.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These lessons in life, these life-skills are, perhaps, even more important.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, our teachers will not shy away and will use these as opportunities to try to turn it into a teachable moment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I do not think we want to give people the impression that we do not want to overprotect our children because we want them to be resilient.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We want to arm our children, put processes in place so that the school can be and continue to be a safe, conducive environment for learning, not just academic learning but also learning of values, behaviours and team work and so on – all the 21st Century Competencies that we think are important for our children to take away into life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And yet, when you have behaviours and interactions, and as I said, there are 400,000 primary and secondary school children, plus minus, if you add the whole system together, ITE, polytechnics and universities, half a million.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And the number of micro interactions is huge.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Really, these are people-to-people relationships and you want a certain degree of resilience, being able to just brush it off and say, "Well, this person, I understand, may have had a bad day".

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But there is a threshold that is not a bright line that is crossed, when that becomes toxic, when that has an impact in a negative way, and when we say we step in, it does not mean we overprotect.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It means we step in to prevent further harm, look at what has happened and make sure that those involved learn, including people who are at the receiving end of the bullying behaviour, to also learn how they can better protect themselves and also understand the spirit of forgiveness.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: And if so, whether such practices may inadvertently incentivise cover-ups, and more importantly, hinder MOE's efforts to send more resources to support these schools.

speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And to the Minister's point about how children actually learn from multiple behaviour sources, which thus highlights the importance of upstream preventative measures, I am very heartened to hear about programmes, like the Parenting for Wellness programme and other tool kits that are available for parents, but more importantly, we also understand that implementation is often times as important as programme and toolkit design.

speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, could the Minister elaborate on what is the uptake rate by parents of the more than 400,000 school-going primary and secondary school children of these toolkits and programmes?

speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And if the uptake rate is low, whether there are other ways to increase this uptake without placing the onus on our teachers that are already burdened trying to manage the situation in school and outside of school?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Well, these CCE changes come about as a result of review.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We had a comprehensive review of the kinds of character and values that we see as important to develop in our children, and we will continue to review these from time to time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And then they are then delivered through pedagogy, through class activities, through student activity, and so on, as well as adult role modelling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And as I said earlier, we hope to be able to also share that with parents so that they can do some reinforcement at home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our parents take charge of our children's upbringing and are also, in a way, teachers of values and character, in as much as our teachers in our classrooms.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As to how we can measure and evaluate, there are so many factors that go into the behaviours of our children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We, of course, can see some of these manifests themselves in the children's relationship with one another, their attitudes towards the people around them, including their teachers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some of these can be seen on the ground.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But I think it is very hard to scientifically measure for each and every child whether these improvements to CCE have, in the short term or immediate term, resulted in certain factors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, the causative link is not so easy to establish, but these are reinforced, these are role-modelled, and we hope that this sets them in a good position and trajectory for life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As for the uptake of the tool kits, I do not have the data at this point in time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I have said, in my reply, that these are made available, our schools disseminate some of this information to our parents as well as to parent support groups.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And we, certainly, as part of this review, want to see how we can improve the material, make it more accessible to diverse audiences and find better and more effective ways to connect with our parents, not just by sharing information, but by working together for our children's well-being and development.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Protecting our young through the prevention and identification of online harms and cyberbullying needs to be a whole-of-community effort.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: In my community engagements with parents, given that the bullying happens to be in the "unseen" online world, I note that many parents were not aware of the extent of their child's cyberbullying cases.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: With online bullying ground movements coming from school backyards, for instance, "XXX", being the school's name, and confessions on social media pages, chat groups, game rooms, how will the school and Ministry reach out to the community to be vigilant to such pages and such movements?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: Beyond the current reporting channels, will the Ministry also consider a nationwide campaign to stamp out cyberbullying in schools, because really, it is not okay to be not okay.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I have called on all Members who filed PQs on this matter for today and the next three days.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The last member I am going to call is Mr Gerald Giam.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You had filed a question for written answer yesterday, but I will allow you to ask another supplementary question.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: How do schools encourage and empower students who are bystanders to intervene and tell the bully that what they are doing is not okay?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The Minister mentioned that students are taught to be upstanders and to respond appropriately to bullying.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can this be made part of the core CCE curriculum and be introduced at a lower primary level?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will be a very important skill that they will carry into adulthood, because bullying can happen at all ages and in all environments.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: That is the end of the MOE question time, almost an hour.
